title: Side-nav & Routing Playbook (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
Drafting a reusable playbook for the console left nav + routing surface. This doc collects: quick wireframe notes, route naming conventions, prioritised backlog items, migration plan, and acceptance criteria for the initial rollouts (beta + GA).

Goals (product + UX):
- Make core routes discoverable and consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private contexts.
- Reduce cognitive load for new users (first 10 mins).
- Allow power users to deep-link to modal states (run -> logs -> token-level trace).
- Support tenancy: admin vs org member vs limited-role views.
- Keep keyboard navigation and screen-reader friendliness as baseline.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We are not changing primary data model or resource ids in this phase. Routing must map to existing resource identifiers.
- No major server-side renames; router-level redirects + alias mapping only.
- Mobile experience reduced-surface: top nav + hamburger for critical actions only (defer full mobile IA to later sprint).

Research notes (quick):
- Support calls: confusion around where 'Model variants' live vs 'Model catalog' (users expect a single place for model configuration).
- SRE/CS requests: make per-request tracing links deterministic (URL params) so support tickets can point to exact UI state.
- Benchmarks: average user session visits 4 unique pages; deep users open 10+ resources via sidebar favorites.

Proposed route taxonomy (canonical names + suggested URL patterns):
- Dashboard: /console or /console/dashboard
- Projects (list): /console/projects  -- project home /console/projects/:projectId
- Models: /console/models  -- model detail /console/models/:modelId
- Endpoints (Hosted / Dedicated): /console/endpoints  -- endpoint detail /console/endpoints/:endpointId
- Jobs / Evals: /console/jobs and /console/evals
- Observability: /console/observability (subroutes: traces, token-costs, per-route metrics)
- Settings: /console/settings (subsections via query or nested routes: /settings/billing, /settings/team)
- Quick-access: /console/shortcuts (bookmarks, pinned dashboards)

Naming rules: kebab-case for paths, human-readable titles in nav, internal route keys use dot.namespace (e.g., nav.models.detail). Keep backwards-compatible aliases in a redirect layer.

Sidebar variants (sketch A/B/C):
- Variant A (Grouped): Primary groups (Observe, Serve, Manage) with section headers. Good for new users to scan.
  - Pros: clarity, scannable. Cons: taller DOM, more clicks for deep nav.
- Variant B (Compact icons + expand on hover): Icon-first compact panel; hover or click to expand labels. Good for power users and small widths.
  - Pros: saves space. Cons: discoverability drop for new users.
- Variant C (Contextual rail): Shows only top-level plus recently-used and pinned items; secondary flyout holds full tree.
  - Pros: customized to user workflows. Cons: more engineering to persist MRU and pins.

Accessibility and keyboard patterns:
- Landmarks: role=navigation wrapper with aria-label="Console sidebar". Each group has aria-labelledby.
- Support roving tabindex for arrow-key traversal and Enter to open.
- Provide skip-to-content anchor for screen readers.
- All icons must have accessible name via aria-hidden=false + visually hidden text.

Wireframe notes (page-by-page):
- Dashboard: large hero area, quick actions (new endpoint, new eval), right-hand pane for alerts. In wireframe: pin last-run jobs into Quick Access.
- Models list: filters (framework, size, quantized), inline actions for 'promote to endpoint'.
- Endpoint detail: Tabs: Overview | Deployments | Traffic | Logs | Traces. Each tab has deep link anchor.
- Observability > Traces: URL should encode traceId and span focus (e.g., ?trace=abc123&focusSpan=45).

Backlog (prioritised, short descriptions, rough t-shirt estimates):
1) CON-421 — router alias layer + redirect rules for old console URLs -> new canonical (Priority: P0, Est: 3d, Owner: frontend).
2) CON-432 — Compact sidebar (variant B) implementation + accessibility (P1, Est: 5d, Owner: frontend + design).
3) CON-438 — 'Pin to sidebar' feature for users (persist in profile) (P1, Est: 4d, Owner: product).
4) CON-445 — Deep-link schema for traces & logs (include query param contract) (P0, Est: 2d, Owner: infra + frontend).
5) CON-449 — RBAC-driven nav visibility (admin vs member) (P1, Est: 6d, Owner: backend + frontend).
6) CON-467 — Quick Access surface with MRU algorithm (experimental) (P2, Est: 8d, Owner: data).
7) CON-470 — Mobile simplified nav + menu accessibility (P2, Est: 4d).

Acceptance criteria (for beta rollout):
- All canonical routes return 200 when visited directly by URL and restore UI state (filters, tabs).
- Keyboard nav passes an a11y check (axe + manual) with no critical violations.
- Redirect layer handles at least 95% of historical inbound links (map from analytics top 50 old URLs).
- RBAC shows/hides items correctly for a matrix of roles (test matrix to be added).

Migration plan (high level):
- Phase 0: Server-side redirect table + QA for top 50 inbound URLs.
- Phase 1: Deploy compact sidebar opt-in behind feature flag; collect telemetry on clicks, time-to-task.
- Phase 2: Make compact default for high-frequency users and enable pinning.
- Phase 3: GA with docs and short product tours.

Telemetry & metrics to observe post-release:
- Time-to-first-action from landing page (goal < 20s).
- Nav bounce rate (users who open console then quickly exit).
- Clicks per session on sidebar items.
- Support tickets referencing "can't find X".

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we expose 'Model variants' under Models or Endpoints? (UX: prefer Models -> variants, Product: prefers under Endpoints). RACI meeting needed.
- Edge-case: What happens to bookmarks using query-only state when backend changes parameter names? Need a compatibility shim.
- Design: Need final iconography set for compact mode (stroke vs filled).

Design tasks for next sprint:
- Create annotated wireframes for all major pages with focus states and animations (owner: Jonas).
- Microcopy pass for pin/unpin flows and onboarding tooltip copy (owner: Lian).

Notes to self / rough thoughts (scratchpad):
- Consider adding a small keyboard quick-jump (Ctrl+K) that opens fuzzy nav and shows pinned + last visited. Can serve as escape hatch while we iterate on sidebar shapes.
- Risk: making default compact could cause increase in support tickets; default opt-in is safer.

Related artifacts (for reviewers):
- Prototype: https://figma.com/file/XXXXXXXX/console-side-nav-v2 (see pages: Compact vs Grouped)
- Jira Epic: JIRA-CON-400 (Console IA revamp)
summary: Working draft with wireframe notes, route taxonomy, sidebar variants, backlog and migration plan for console IA refactor.
